notes: glmmTMB help example owls_nb1 (nbinom1, zero-inflation ~1; Zuur et al. 2009). BroodSize enters as offset(log(BroodSize)) but is a model column, listed under covariates (gopher rule). NegPerChick (=SiblingNegotiation/BroodSize) and logBroodSize (=log(BroodSize)) are derived, ignored; ArrivalTime is an unused usable column. The update owls_nb1_bs moves the offset to a log(BroodSize) covariate, not filed as a second model.
glmmTMB help example zipm3 (Poisson, zero-inflation ~spp*mined; Price et al. 2016, Dryad doi 10.5061/dryad.5m8f6). cover, sample, DOP, Wtemp and DOY are unused usable covariates left as columns.

glmmTMB help example fm (nbinom2; Booth et al. 2003). Extended version of MASS::epil (different source; cross-source duplicate left to the merge). Base=log(base/4), Age=log(age), Visit=(period-2.5)/5 are the modelled transforms, so raw base/age/period plus lbase/lage (MASS transforms) and V4 (4th-visit indicator) are derived and ignored. subject coerced to factor in the example.

formula: abund ~ soil.dry + bare.sand + fallen.leaves + moss + herb.layer + reflection + (1|id) + (1|Species)
notes: Help page gives no model (CANOCO spider data in long form, via mvabund). RULE GAP: model rendered from the design at low; abund (count) response, environmental variables (log-transformed per CANOCO) as site-level covariates, id (site) and Species inferred as crossed random intercepts from the column names and the known 28-site 12-species spider data.

brms help example fit2 (Poisson, varying patient intercepts; Breslow & Clayton 1993, Thall & Vail 1990). fit1 has no random effect, not filed. zAge/zBase are the standardized Age/Base the model uses, so Age and Base are ignored; obs is the row id; visit (1-4) is an unused usable time column.

brms help example fit2 (cumulative ordinal, varying subject intercepts; Ezzet & Whitehead 1991). rating is a 1-4 ordinal rating (stored numeric). fit1 (sratio, no random effect) not filed. treat/period/carry are the two-period crossover contrasts.

brms help example fit2 (Weibull frailty, varying patient intercepts; McGilchrist & Aisbett 1991). RULE GAP: censored survival response (time | cens(censored)), not a standard GLMM; filed for the patient grouping, response_type continuous (survival time), the censored indicator ignored. recur (1st/2nd recurrence) is an unused usable column.

formula: cum ~ compartmental reserving growth curve ult*(1-exp(-(dev/theta)^omega)) over development month dev; origin-year-specific ult via (1|AY); omega and theta fixed
notes: NONLINEAR: brms help example fit_loss (Gaussian nonlinear; Gesmann & Morris 2020, hierarchical compartmental reserving). Cumulative loss cum grows with development month dev; ult has an origin-year random intercept (1|AY); omega and theta are fixed scalars. premium is an unused usable column. Confidence capped at medium by the nonlinear rule.

Help page gives no model (A-not-A-with-sureness discrimination design; Christensen, Cleaver & Brockhoff 2011). Model recalled at medium from that paper and the ordinal package clmm worked example: ordered 6-level SURENESS ~ PROD with random respondent intercept (1|RESP). PRODID, DAY, SOUPTYPE, SOUPFREQ, COLD, EASY, GENDER, AGEGROUP and LOCATION are unused usable covariates. Domain psychology_neuroscience for the perceptual discrimination task (reporting only; Unilever consumer research, could read as industry).

Help page fits clm(rating ~ temp*contact) with no random effect. RULE GAP: that model has no grouping factor, so the registered model is the judge random-intercept version recalled from Tutz & Hennevogl (1996) and the ordinal clmm worked example. rating is the ordered 5-level grouping of the continuous column response (ignored). bottle (8 levels) is an unused usable column. Domain industry for the wine-production process factors (reporting only; could read as agriculture).

geepack help example fit (ordgee, exchangeable). The source fits a GEE; its cluster id is the grouping factor, given here as the lme4-equivalent random intercept (1|id). y is an ordered 3-level response; day is modelled as a factor. Ordinal Data from Koch.

formula: numobese ~ gender + cage + cage2 + gender:cage + gender:cage2 + (1|id)
notes: geepack help example gee2 (geeglm, binomial, independence). The source fits a GEE; cluster id given as (1|id) (Woolson & Clarke 1984; Fitzmaurice ALA). numobese (0/1) response; obese is its yes/no twin, ignored. Formula verbatim uses cage=age-12 and cage2=cage^2 (derived from age), so the age polynomial reduces to the column age. occasion (wave) and base_age are unused usable columns. gee1 (numobese~gender) not filed as a second model.

geepack help example fit.ex (geeglm, binomial, exchangeable). The source fits a GEE; cluster id given as (1|id) (Fitzmaurice & Laird 1993). resp is binary wheeze status; age is centred at 9 years. A subset of the external six-city study (kept, not a same-source derivation).

geepack help example gee.exc (geeglm, binomial, exchangeable). The source fits a GEE; cluster id given as (1|id); 111 patients from two clinics. outcome is binary respiratory status. center is a fixed covariate as modelled (not a random effect); sex and visit are unused usable columns. The aliased respiratoryWide is not a separately enumerated object.

geepack help example geese fits fit.88/fit.89 (GEE, AR1) with cluster id = tree (Diggle, Liang & Zeger 1994); the survey adds the chamber the trees sit in (four chambers, ozone assigned at chamber level, so chamber inference is weak; spot check #22). contr=1-(ozone==enriched) is derived from ozone; the example splits spruce into sitka88 (wave<=5) and sitka89 (wave>5), the survey uses the full table. Confidence medium for the lme4 translation of the subset GEE fits.

Help page gives no model (only coplot/qplot of Weight~Time faceted by Evit*Cu; Lauridsen et al. 1999). RULE GAP: model rendered at low from the 3x3 factorial weekly-growth design; Weight (continuous) on Time, Evit and Cu with pig random intercepts, pigs nested in litters ((1|Litter)+(1|Pig)). Feed (cumulated intake) and Start (week-1 weight) are unused usable columns. Second reading #22: Start (weight at the start) is a baseline covariate.
